Name: South Park ontology, in SDLAF
Description: Jessica Talisman's South Park ontology as an ordinary rulebook: her ten stated facts are rows and columns of the tables they are about (people, parenthoods, marriages, friendships, grade and role records), and each of her five rules is a field: the inverse is the parenthood read from the child's end, the symmetric rule a link with no direction counted from both ends, the property chain a lookup through two parenthoods, domain and range a formula and a count on each individual, disjointness a check on each parenthood. Every rule is switched by the one Reasoning row. Nothing is a generic subject-property-object store: Schema, Data, Lookups, Aggregations and Formulas only.

schema.Description: The metadata key. Unique within the table.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Order 1. Mirrors MetaKey so the row is addressable by Name.

schema.name: ValueType
schema.Description: How to read the value: 'string' uses StringValue, 'object' or 'array' parse JsonValue.

schema.name: StringValue
schema.Description: The value when ValueType is 'string'.

schema.name: JsonValue
schema.Description: The value as JSON when ValueType is 'object' or 'array'.

data.StringValue: Talisman's South Park ontology, as Schema, Data, Lookups, Aggregations and Formulas
data.Name: title

data.StringValue: Character and location portraits are Fandom images, linked from each Things row; South Park is the work of Trey Parker and Matt Stone.
data.Name: image_credit

data.StringValue: The data is her page's ten built-in facts as the page starts. Her page starts with every rule switched off; here the one Reasoning row switches them all on, so every conclusion shows. The ontology form of the same world is ../effortless-rulebook/.
data.Name: reference_note

Reasoning.Description: The one world the rules reason over, and the switch of each of her five rules. Every table links here, so each rule's switch is one lookup away from the field it gates, and every count of the world rolls up here.

schema.name: ReasoningId
schema.Description: Key of the world.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Order 1. The world's name.

schema.name: Label
schema.Description: The world's name.

schema.name: InverseIsOn
schema.Description: Inverse rule: a parent link also gives a child link between the same two people (isChildOf, the inverse of isParentOf).

schema.name: SymmetricIsOn
schema.Description: Symmetric rule: a spouse link or a friend link holds for both people.

schema.name: ChainIsOn
schema.Description: Property chain: a parent of a parent is a grandparent (isParentOf then isParentOf gives isGrandparentOf).

schema.name: DomainRangeIsOn
schema.Description: Domain and range: whoever attends something, or has a grade level or a role, is a Person; whatever is attended is a School.

schema.name: DisjointIsOn
schema.Description: Disjoint: no one is both the parent and the spouse of the same person (isParentOf is disjoint with isSpouseOf).

schema.Description: Order 1. Every individual of the world.

schema.name: CountOfPeople
schema.Description: Order 3. Individuals that are a Person, asserted or concluded.

schema.name: CountOfSchools
schema.Description: Order 3. Individuals that are a School, asserted or concluded.

schema.name: CountOfStatedParenthoods

schema.name: CountOfCurrentRoles
schema.Description: Order 3. Role facts in effect: each person's current role.

schema.name: CountOfStatedFacts
schema.Description: Order 4. Every stated fact in effect, wherever it is held.

schema.name: CountOfChildOfConclusions
schema.Description: Order 2. isChildOf facts the inverse rule concludes: one per parenthood.

schema.name: CountOfMirroredMarriages
schema.Description: Order 2. isSpouseOf facts the symmetric rule concludes: one per marriage, read from its second partner.

schema.name: CountOfMirroredFriendships
schema.Description: Order 2. isFriendOf facts the symmetric rule concludes: one per friendship, read from its second friend.

schema.name: CountOfGrandparentConclusions
schema.Description: Order 4. isGrandparentOf facts the property chain concludes.

schema.name: CountOfPersonConclusions
schema.Description: Order 3. Individuals the domain rule makes a Person that no one asserted was one.

schema.name: CountOfSchoolConclusions
schema.Description: Order 3. Individuals the range rule makes a School that no one asserted was one.

schema.name: CountOfConclusions
schema.Description: Order 5. Every fact the rules conclude that no one stated.

schema.name: CountOfContradictions
schema.Description: Order 4. Parenthoods the disjoint rule flags: the parent is also the child's spouse.

schema.name: IsConsistent

schema.name: Summary
schema.Description: Order 6. The world in one line.

Individuals.Description: Every individual of the world (owl:Thing). What is said about one individual alone is a column of its row: its age, the place it attends, whether it is asserted to be a Person or a School. Its current grade level and role come from their records. Class membership is a formula, not a table, because it is concluded: no one stated that South Park Elementary is a School.

schema.name: ChildCount

Parenthoods.Description: One row per stated isParentOf fact. A person has many children and a child more than one parent, so the link is its own entity with two links to Individuals. The inverse rule's isChildOf is not stored: it is this row read from the child's end.

schema.name: Name

schema.name: DisjointIsOn
schema.Description: Order 1. The Disjoint rule's switch, read from the reasoning this row belongs to.

schema.name: ChildOfHolds
schema.Description: Order 2. The inverse rule concludes the child is child of the parent. Open world: true, or not known.

schema.name: ChildOfSentence
schema.Description: Order 2. The inverse fact in words.

schema.name: SpouseAsStatedCount
schema.Description: Order 3. Marriages stated with the parent first and the child second.

schema.name: SpouseAsMirroredCount
schema.Description: Order 3. Marriages stated with the child first, which make the parent the child's spouse when the symmetric rule mirrors them.

schema.name: IsContradiction

schema.name: AncestryClosure

Grandparenthoods.Description: The property chain isParentOf then isParentOf, as rows: every ordered pair of parenthoods is a candidate, and it holds when the first one's child is the second one's parent. A formula cannot add a row, so the candidates are data (every pair, decided by nothing about the family) and whether one holds is a formula.

schema.name: GrandparenthoodId
schema.Description: Key: the upper parenthood, then the lower one.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Order 4. The concluded fact in words, or why this pair concludes nothing.
schema.formula: =IF({{Links}}, CONCAT({{GrandparentLabel}}, " is grandparent of ", {{GrandchildLabel}}), CONCAT("(", {{UpperLink}}, " does not lead to ", {{LowerLink}}, ")"))

schema.name: Reasoning
schema.Description: The world this candidate belongs to.

schema.name: UpperLink
schema.Description: The first link: grandparent to the middle generation.

schema.name: LowerLink
schema.Description: The second link: the middle generation to the grandchild.

schema.name: Grandparent
schema.Description: Order 1. The upper link's parent.

schema.name: UpperChild
schema.Description: Order 1. The upper link's child.

schema.name: LowerParent
schema.Description: Order 1. The lower link's parent.

schema.name: Grandchild
schema.Description: Order 1. The lower link's child.

schema.name: GrandparentLabel
schema.Description: Order 2. The grandparent's name.

schema.name: GrandchildLabel
schema.Description: Order 2. The grandchild's name.

schema.name: Links
schema.Description: Order 2. The upper link's child is the lower link's parent: the two links make a chain.

schema.name: ChainIsOn
schema.Description: Order 1. The Chain rule's switch, read from the reasoning this row belongs to.

schema.name: Holds
schema.Description: Order 3. The property chain concludes isGrandparentOf. Open world: true, or not known.
